headline: Approved a 205-unit development at 41 Hurd Street and continued the new home at 675 Andover Street to December 14.
summary: Approved a repair to the Upper Pawtucket Canal Wall at 706 Broadway Street and a historic permit for 353 Wilder Street. Also approved a historic designation for 37 Lee Street and a preservation restriction for the Bigelow Lowell Building. Presentations on a 10-story building at 5.1 Thorndike St and the Kerouac Center were informational.
decisions: Approved the historic permit for 353 Wilder Street with a standard order of conditions, 5-0.
Continued the historic permit for a new home at 675 Andover Street to the December 14 meeting, 5-0.
Approved the historic permit to demolish the existing building and build a 205-unit mixed-use development at 41 Hurd Street, 5-0.
Approved the repair of the Upper Pawtucket Canal Wall at 706 Broadway Street, with a condition that the mortar joints be provided to the Board, 5-0.
Appointed T. Depeiza as the Historic Board representative on the Community Preservation Committee, 5-0.
Designated 37 Lee Street as historic and significant to the City of Lowell, 5-0.
Approved orders to appear for 295 Dutton St and 1 Merrimack St, 5-0.
Accepted the Preservation Restriction for the Bigelow Lowell Building at 246.2 Market Street, 5-0.

plain_text:
LOWELL HISTORIC BOARD  
MINUTES  
Mayor’s Reception Room, Lowell City Hall  
October 19, 2026 at 6:00 p.m.  
  
Note: These minutes are not completed verbatim. For further detail, contact the Lowell Historic 
Board, Lowell City Hall, Room 51, 375 Merrimack Street or refer to video recordings available online 
at www.LTC.org.  
  
Members Present:  Chair George Villaras, Vice Chair Jeffrey Harris, Yovani Baez-Rose, Troy 
Depeiza, Aurora Erickson 
         
Members Absent:  Member Gray Fitzimons, Member Lucia Walker, Member Deborah Belanger  
  
Others Present:  Dylan Ricker, Senior Planner  
  
The following represents the actions taken by the Historic Board at the 10/19/26 meeting.   
  
Chair Villaras called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.  
 
 
A quorum of the Board was present. Chair Villaras called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM 
 
I. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
A. WSND-27-1: 353 Wilder Street 
An application for a Historic Permit has been submitted by ASG Construction Corporation to 
demolish a portion of the existing structure at 353 Wilder Street. The applicant reports the 
portion of the existing structure is compromised. The applicant plans to construct a new 
structure in place of the demolished portion of the building. The property is located within the 
Wilder Street Neighborhood District, and requires a Major Development permit from the Lowell 
Historic Board for demolition of an existing structure. 
 
On Behalf: 
Brendan Conley, Applicant 
 
B. Conley explained the updated architectural plans for the addition to 353 Wilder St. B. Conley 
said the ZBA and Planning Board have approved the proposal. B. Conley said the quoins on the 
facade were removed and more symmetry was added with windows on the street facing 
elevation.  
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion:
J. Harris acknowledged the efforts to work on the symmetry of the windows and removal of the 
quoins and said the new design is more compatible with the neighborhood.  
 
Motion: 
J. Harris motioned to approve with a standard order of conditions, T. Depeiza seconded the 
motion. The motion passed unanimously, (5-0). 
 
 
B. ASND-27-1: 675 Andover Street 
An application for a Historic Permit has been submitted by Kevin & Debbie Fernandes to 
construct a new single-family at 675 Andover Street. The subject property is located in the 
Andover Street Neighborhood Historic District. The project requires a Major Development 
permit from the Lowell Historic Board for new construction. 
 
On Behalf: 
John Geary, Applicant’s Representative 
 
J. Geary introduced the project and team working on the project. J. Geary explained the 
proposed lot layout, and proposed home. J. Geary said the applicant is scheduled to appear 
before the Planning Board where they will require 3 Special Permits. 
 
J. Geary said setbacks vary on the street and said the home will face Andover Street. J. Geary 
said he believes they meet the requirements. J. Geary said the massing and scaling is consistent 
with the existing massing in the area. J. Geary said the materials are consistent with new 
construction in the district. 
 
AD Sullivan, Applicant’s Architect 
 
A. Sullivan explained the size of the home. A. Sullivan said the home is a traditional New England 
farmhouse with revival elements. A. Sullivan said the homes in the area are unique from one 
another, but each home fits. A. Sullivan said the applicant worked with S. Stowell on designs.  
 
Matt Hamor, Applicant’s Engineer 
 
M. Hamor explained the lot layout. M. Hamor explained the proposed driveway entrance to the 
site and described the building layout. M. Hamor said a drainage system will be included on the 
site. 
 
Angie Verge, Applicant’s Landscape Architect 
 
A. Verge said they are proposing native plants, and said they are proposing native shade trees, 
including red oak and red maples. A. Verge said they would be planting 2 to 2.5 inch caliper 
trees. A. Verge said evergreen screening trees will be installed at 7 to 8 ft height. A. Verge said 
as many of the trees as possible will remain. A. Verge said the majority of trees on site are 
Norway Maples which are invasive. A. Verge said a solid panel privacy fence is proposed as a 
wood grain vinyl product with a cedar finish. A. Verge said low retaining walls will be used.  
 
In Favor:
Elise Bemmer, Hovey Street 
 
E. Bemmer expressed support for the proposed home. E. Bemmer said she appreciates the 
historic character of Belvidere. E. Bemmer said thoughtful design can enhance neighborhoods. 
E. Bemmer said she believes the home fits with the architecture of the neighborhood.  
 
Magaly Ronan, 880 Andover Street 
 
M. Ronan said after getting more information on the project she is no longer opposed to the 
project and is now in support after speaking with the homeowners. M. Ronan expressed support 
for the project. 
 
Natalie Remonstera, 79 Virginia Ave 
 
N. Remonstera said she has known the applicants for a longtime and said they are good 
neighbors. N. Remonstera said she reviewed the plans and expressed support. N. Remonstera 
said it will be a wonderful addition to the neighborhood. 
 
John Vega,  
 
J. Vega said he walked the neighborhood and reviewed the plan. J. Vega said it fits with the 
neighborhood and said the architecture blends with the neighborhood. J. Vega expressed 
support. 
 
Susannah Martins, 17 Alice Dr 
 
S. Martins said the applicant has taken great care to design a property that keeps in the overall 
feel of the district. S. Martins expressed support for the plans, and said it fits in well with the 
surrounding neighborhood. S. Martins noted various designs and lot sizes in the area.  
 
Walter McGrail, 137 Belmont Ave 
 
W. McGrail said the design will fit into the area, and noted there are other recent homes in the 
area. W. McGrail said it would be a welcome addition to the City.  
 
John Krapian , 174 Belmont Ave 
 
J. Krapian said the design fits into the neighborhood, and said he would be happy to see it built. 
J. Krapian expressed support. 
 
In Opposition: 
Peter Finnegan, 21 Garden Rd 
 
P. Finnegan said he has a 100-year-old home. P. Finnegan said when he initially spoke with the 
neighbor he indicated he was not planning on building a home at the location. P. Finnegan said 
he later found out he had been planning to build a home. P. Finnegan said the builder has a 
record of flipping homes.
Grant Garbach, 688 Andover Street 
 
G. Garbach said the historic district and quality of life is why he chose Lowell. G. Garbach said 
the driveway is very long and does not meet code. G. Garbach said the home has one of the 
larger setbacks in the neighborhood. G. Garbach noted public trees would need to be removed. 
G. Garbach said there is no tree inventory list or arborist or tree permit. G. Garbach said the 
project does not fit within the neighborhood. G. Garbach said neighbors are widely opposed to 
the petition. G. Garbach said the setback is an outlier. G. Garbach said the home is 60 ft further 
setback than any other home in the district. G. Garbach said the home does not relate to the 
street since it is so far setback. G. Garbach said the proposal is a flag lot which is unprecedented 
in this historic district. G. Garbach recommended the Board deny the petition. 
 
Erin Marshall, 26 Douglas Rd 
 
E. Marshall expressed opposition and said she agrees with Grant. 
 
David Slattery, 130 Glenwood Street 
 
D. Slattery expressed opposition. D. Slattery said his concern is the impact on the historic 
character and integrity of the district. D. Slattery said surrounding properties contribute to the 
area’s historic identity. D. Slattery said the proposal is overdevelopment. D. Slattery said the 
construction is inconsistent with the intent of the historic district. D. Slattery expressed concern 
about setbacks and nearby homes. D. Slattery expressed concern with groundwater issues, and 
said new construction will negatively impact their homes. D. Slattery said he is concerned with 
the loss of open space. D. Slattery expressed opposition to the project.  
 
Brian Barry, 85 Clark Rd 
 
B. Barry said he submitted written comment as well. B. Barry said his understanding was the City 
no longer permitted flag lots. B. Barry said the home is not like any other homes in the historic 
district. B. Barry said the lot only has 18 ft width at one point, and said it does not fit into the 
neighborhood. 
 
Cornelia Demers Sborov, 15 Garden Rd 
 
C. Demers-Sborov said the driveway is actually proposed to enter at an angle and will cause 
headlights to shine into an abutting home. C. Demers-Sborov said there will be light and noise 
nuisance. C. Demers-Sborov said she does not believe the drawing is to scale. C. Demers-Sborov 
said she submitted a report explaining the concerns of the neighborhood. C. Demers-Sborov said 
she is concerned about their property values and said there is no landscaping to protect the 
neighbors on Garden Road. C. Demers-Sborov said the existing home has problems already due 
to industrial strength lights shining on the property now, and it is impacting their ability to sleep 
at night. C. Demers-Sborov said she believes it is a wetland, and said there is a high water table. 
C. Demers-Sborov expressed concern about flooding in her basement. C. Demers-Sborov said if 
it is a wetland the stormwater system will not work. C. Demers-Sborov expressed opposition. 
 
Djwan Scott, 11 Garden Rd (683 Andover St)
D. Scott expressed opposition. D. Scott said she has not seen anywhere at the property since it 
was sold. D. Scott expressed concerns about ponding, and water runoff. D. Scott expressed 
concerns with Conservation. D. Scott said it will detract from the neighborhood. D. Scott 
expressed opposition. 
 
Caitlin Thurston, 36 Douglas Rd 
 
C. Thurston said she has concerns related to water runoff. C. Thurston said she has seen an 
intermittent stream. C. Thurston said the construction will cause water into the basements. C. 
Thurston said there is a concern with emergency vehicle access. C. Thurston requested the 
Board deny the petition.  
 
Neal Boisonneault, 678 Andover Street 
 
N. Boisonneault said the home would not impact his home directly. N. Boisonneault said the 
project is not neighborly. N. Boisonneault said a lot of relief is needed for the home. N. 
Boisonneault said snow removal will cause the driveway to become more crowded during 
winter.  
 
Kristy McCabe, 665 Andover Street 
 
K. McCabe said they are in close proximity to the Worcester House, the most historic home in 
the district. K. McCabe expressed concern the design and placement is not compatible with the 
historic surroundings. K. McCabe said the home does not respect the historic district. K. McCabe 
expressed concern about the impact on their property and the neighborhood. K. McCabe urged 
the Board to deny the project.  
 
Discussion: 
A. Erickson clarified that the Historic Board’s purview is just the Historic, and noted that many 
items raised are not for this Board to address. A. Erickson said they are here only to address the 
historic elements, and said other boards can address the other concerns.  
 
J. Harris asked how the driveway will be laid out due to inconsistency in plans. M. Hamor said 
the original plan had a driveway straight in but that was revised to come in at an angle to not 
impact 2 existing trees. J. Harris clarified that 2 of the street trees could be saved with the 
change. J. Harris asked if there is a location for a street tree. M. Hamor said 2 shade trees could 
be added to the lot with the existing home for compensation. J. Harris said the shade trees are 
major piece of the character of Andover Street. M. Hamor said a replacement is typically a 2 in 
dbh replacement. 
 
G. Villaras asked about the driveway plantings along the left side of the property, and asked if 
additional plantings could be added. M. Hamor agreed. J. Harris asked if a site plan is available 
that shows the existing conditions including where existing trees are located. M. Hamor said a 
full inventory was not done on the property. M. Hamor said a new plan can be submitted that 
can show a better visual of what will be lost. J. Harris said the additional plan would give the 
Board a better idea of what is being lost.
G. Villaras asked if there are any other similarly developed properties, and said it would be 
helpful to see how this fits in with the past development. J. Geary said the applicant would be 
happy to provide this additional info. J. Harris echoed that having a rendering from Andover 
Street would be helpful to understand the visual impact of the home. G. Villaras said the type of 
construction it would beneficial. J. Geary agreed.  
 
Y. Baez-Rose noted the home faces the backyard of another home, and asked if there are other 
examples of this in the district. Y. Baez-Rose asked if this is seen in any of the other historic 
districts. Y. Baez-Rose said she is unsure if this type of development has been permitted in any 
other district. J. Geary said they can provide examples, J. Geary noted a property around 330 
Andover Street, and noted 133 Clark Rd which had a home built in the backyard. J. Geary said 
the zoning code allows for these homes to be created when there is greater than 20,000 sq ft. J. 
Geary said he can provide that information to the Board. 
 
Y. Baez-Rose noted members are not likely ready to vote tonight, and said additional submitted 
info is public and will be discussed at a future meeting. 
 
G. Villaras said he needs a few more questions answered. G. Villaras recommended a 
continuance. J. Geary requested Dec 14th. 
 
J. Harris asked if the infiltration trench is on both sides of the property and asked for the width. 
M. Hamor said it is 1.5 ft and only on one side of the driveway. J. Harris asked why the trench is 
necessary. M. Hamor said it is to mitigate driveway runoff.  J. Harris said he has concerns about 
the aesthetics of the infiltration trench in the Andover Street district. J. Harris recommended 
looking toward grass or a vegetated swaile. M. Hamor agreed to look into this. 
 
A. Erickson said she’d like more info on the historic context of this lot, and how long it has been 
wooded.  
 
J. Harris added the driveways in close proximity is an atypical scenario for the district. J. Harris 
recommended a shared driveway arrangement with the existing driveway so there is only 1 
curbcut along Andover Street. J. Geary said they will review that.  
 
Motion: 
J. Harris motioned to continue to 12/14 meeting, Y. Baez-Rose seconded the motion. The 
motion passed unanimously, (5-0). 
 
 
C. DLHD-27-15: 41 Hurd Street 
An application for a Historic Permit has been submitted by New England Heritage Properties, Inc 
to demolish the existing building, and construct a new 205-unit mixed-use development at 41 
Hurd Street. The property is located in the Downtown Lowell Historic District. The project 
requires a Major Development permit for demolition and new construction. 
 
On Behalf: 
John Geary, Applicant’s Representative
J. Geary summarized the proposal. J. Geary said the plan is to demo the existing building and 
construct a new 205-unit mixed use development. J. Geary said the applicant has submitted the 
archival report for the project. J. Geary said the request is based on feasibility and said the 
property as it exists would not yield enough units to be financeable. J. Geary said the project 
meets the City goals for housing while being sensitive to the Downtown Lowell Historic District. 
J. Geary said the design is compatible with the surrounding buildings. J. Geary said the applicant 
did a site visit with Board members and staff and identified features to be incorporated into the 
new building.  
 
Jeff Bush, Applicant 
 
J. Bush said he is excited to move this project forward and said they are happy to work with the 
Board. 
 
Aubrey Bennett, Applicant’s Architect 
 
A. Bennett explained how the plans were revised to address the initial concerns of the Historic 
Board. A. Bennett explained the other buildings in the district that relate to the proposed plans. 
A. Bennett explained the proposed layout for the amenity spaces that the historic features of 
the courthouse will be incorporated into the new building. A. Bennett said the skylight could be 
incorporated in the gardens as a pergola and the medallion could be incorporated into the 
gardens with a plaque explaining its reasoning in the current building. 
 
A. Bennett said the wall was revised to increase the height to hide the parking area, and a railing 
as an arch to relate to existing building. A. Bennett said precast elements were added to the 
columns. A. Bennett said adding the arch into the railing design and the railing on the building 
provides an additional purpose. 
 
A. Bennett explained how the property appears from the Central St corridor, and presented the 
renderings from Central St. A. Bennett noted the materials relate to the buildings on the Central 
St corridor.  
 
J. Geary said the applicant did their best to address the concerns from the previous hearing. J. 
Geary said they believe they meet the requirements for the Historic Permit. 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None 
 
Discussion: 
J. Harris thanked the applicant for the tour of the building and helped better understand the 
nature of the building, and thanked the applicant for incorporating these items into the design 
of the new building. 
 
J. Harris said he feels the tweaks to the design, the wall in particular, are successful  and the 
additional vegetation is successful. J. Harris said the efforts to incorporate elements of the old
courthouse are successful and noted the arch elements are subtle but make good reference. J. 
Harris said he would want to look closely at the fixtures for the light fixtures on the wall and 
noted the difference between the lighting on the building and wall, and recommended more 
contemporary lighting along the wall to match the lighting on the building. J. Harris said that can 
be reviewed at staff level. 
 
T. Depeiza expressed support for the plans, and said the building fits architecturally into the 
district. T. Depeiza said it would be interesting to see how the site would look at night, and said 
the updates were successful. 
 
Y. Baez-Rose said the applicant did a good job responding to the concerns of the informational. 
Y. Baez-Rose said the project is consistent with what was requested when the property was 
listed for disposition. Y. Baez-Rose said the development will compliment the neighborhood and 
meets the expectations for this project. Y. Baez-Rose expressed support. 
 
A. Erickson said she is hesitant to approve demolitions but understands that not every building 
can be saved. A. Erickson expressed support for the revision to the plans and said the 
collaborative process helped improve the project.  
 
G. Villaras thanked the applicant for providing the revised design and said his concerns with wall 
were addressed and said he is supportive of the new wall design. G. Villaras said the building 
connects well with the area, and said he is supportive of the design. 
 
Motion: 
Y. Baez-Rose motioned to approve, T. Depeiza seconded the motion. The motion passed 
unanimously, (5-0). 
 
D. DLHD-27-16: 706 Broadway Street 
An application for Historic Permit has been submitted by Boott Hydropower, LLC to repair an 
approximately 35-foot long portion of the Upper Pawtucket Canal Wall at 706 Broadway Street. 
THe property is located in the Downtown Lowell Historic District. The project requires a Major 
Development Permit pursuant to the Lowell Historic District Act. 
 
On Behalf: 
Morgan Marlow, Applicant’s Representative 
 
M. Marlow said the proposal is to replace the portion of the canal wall that failed. M. Marlow 
said they have 3 repair alternatives all with the goal of maintaining the aesthetic of the wall. M. 
Marlow explained the 3 alternatives. M. Marlow said the preferred alternative is the stone 
masonry retaining wall for a constructability perspective. M. Marlow noted Mass Historical 
reviewed and deemed no adverse effect. 
 
In Favor: 
None 
 
In Opposition: 
None
Discussion: 
J. Harris asked about the cause of the collapse of the wall. M. Marlow said they suspect the wall 
failed due to vegetation, possibly a tree growing out of the wall, and said there is stored 
material near the wall contributed to the wall failure. M. Marlow said the material storage is 
brought into consideration because it may be adding a load to the wall that is not in other areas.  
 
J. Harris asked if the continued storage of materials is a threat to the new wall. M. Marlow said 
the new wall would not be at threat. M. Marlow said the applicant is considering a conversation 
with the property owner related to materials storage. M. Marlow said they will have these 
conversations with the business.  
 
J. Harris noted the design matches what was there historically, and expressed support. J. Harris 
asked the mortar lines be placed further back to match existing wall. M. Marlow agreed, and 
added they will repurpose the stone that fell and these pieces will be at the front of the wall. 
 
G. Villaras asked if extra stone is needed. M. Marlow said the if enough existing stone can be 
used for the face of the wall then the new stone would not be visible. M. Marlow said it is an 18 
ft wall and water line is only a few feet high. 
 
Motion: 
J. Harris motioned to approve with the condition that the mortar joints be provided to the 
Board, Y. Baez-Rose seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously, (5-0). 
 
II. MINUTES 
 
Approval of the July 13, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
T. Depeiza motioned to approve, Y. Baez-Rose seconded the motion. The motion passed unanimously, 
(5-0). 
 
 
III. OTHER BUSINESS 
 
A. Informational Presentation: 5.1 Thorndike St 
 
On Behalf: 
Kevin Murphy, Applicant’s Representative 
 
K. Murphy said the parcel is on the outskirts of the historic district. K. Murphy said the only way 
the project works is with a 10-story building. K. Murphy said there is precedence and cited the 
River Place Towers that is 19 stories. K. Murphy said the project will be difficult to market due to 
the surrounding area. K. Murphy said 10 stories is the only way to make the building feasible 
financially. K. Murphy said the project fits into the MBTA communities legislation and noted its 
proximity to the Gallagher Terminal. K. Murphy said they will continue to work with the Board 
on the materials  but noted the height of the building is paramount.  
 
Matt Hamor, Applicant’s Representative 
M. Hamor presented the rendering showing the proposed building from the Thorndike Street 
intersection. M. Hamor said this was provided in addition to the other renderings. M. Hamor
explained the site layout. M. Hamor explained the renderings from different areas of the City 
showing the proposed building.  
 
AD Sullivan, Applicant’s Architect 
 
A. Sullivan said they had met with S. Stowell about the development, and they wanted to create 
a base that felt like old Lowell with something new coming out of the base. A. Sullivan explained 
the design. 
 
Michael Farris, Applicant 
 
M. Farris said they have been working on the project for a while now. M. Farris said he reviewed 
the economic feasibility of the project. M. Farris said the 10 stories is necessary to make the 
project feasible, M. Farris said the 3 additional stories provide enough units to make the 
development work. M. Farris said to address the fixed costs they need additional stories. M. 
Farris said the building is set so low that it does not feel like a 10 story building.  
 
Discussion: 
G. Villaras expressed support for the colors, and said the project fits well within the space. G. 
Villaras said materials would still need to be reviewed, but said he appreciates the work done on 
the design. 
 
A. Erickson asked about the balcony like item on the facade. A. Sullivan said he believes it is a 
stepback for the top 2 floors which needed to be setback, and said the structure is a deck. Y. 
Baez-Rose asked if it is a usable deck. A. Sullivan confirmed it is usable. M. Hamor noted the 
different steps in the property.  
 
J. Harris asked if the height or design changed since the last hearing. M. Hamor said it has not 
changed. M. Hamor said the additional perspective was provided from the prior review. J. Harris 
noted the property is unique, but added there are historic considerations for the site. J. Harris 
said given the elevation of the site a taller building could be done in a way that keeps with the 
character of the district. J. Harris said the building is much larger than other buildings and does 
too much to change the character of the district. J. Harris noted that other sites have different 
contexts. J. Harris expressed concerns about the development. 
 
Y. Baez-Rose noted there was a public process that lead to a zoning overlay that allowed for 
taller buildings to be built at this area. Y. Baez-Rose noted it was a public process that created a 
district that also touches this Board’s purview and noted the Board was not vocally opposed at 
that time. Y. Baez-Rose said she understands the importance of historic context but noted it is a 
changing community and noted other requirements allow buildings of this scale. Y. Baez-Rose 
said there may be similar developments that come forward in the future as well. 
 
G. Villaras asked if the original intent of the HCD was to have a taller signature building. Y. Baez-
Rose confirmed it is her understanding a roughly 14 story building was meant to be the 
signature building of the district. Y. Baez-Rose added that has a form based code which is 
different from MBTA overlays but notes it has its own unique regulations.
A. Erickson said the locations on the edge of the district are more challenging. A. Erickson said 
she is concerned about the precedent that is created in the district by approving this proposal.  
 
T. Depeiza said the elevation would be interesting to see from the side profile. T. Depeiza said 
the building is well designed, but the height is an issue to grapple with.  
 
B. Informational Presentation: Kerouac Center 
 
On Behalf: 
Kent Kovacs, Applicant’s Representative 
 
Jim Sampas, CEO of Jack Kerouac Foundation 
 
J. Sampas stated they have been working to create the Kerouac Center at the old St Jean 
Baptiste Church. J. sampas said Jack is one of the most influential people to come from Lowell 
and their goal is to create a center that will attract a worldwide audience. J. Sampas said they 
have contracted an internationally known architect to work on the design for the building.  
 
Kent Kovacs, Applicant’s Representative 
 
K. Kovacs said the goal of the project is help maintain the existing building and incorporate this 
into the final design. K. Kovacs said the final design maintains the initial use of the space as an 
area for people to gather. K. Kovacs said addition is to serve as the museum to Jack Kerouac. K. 
Kovacs explained the existing and proposed conditions. K. Kovacs explained the proposed floor 
plans for the site. K. Kovacs said as much mechanical and electrical will be within the building as 
possible. K. Kovacs said the addition will include the museum which will house the Kerouac scroll 
and the elevators for ADA accessibility. K. Kovacs said there is global investment now. K. Kovacs 
said the lower level of the addition will be attached and showcase the exterior wall of the 
church. K. Kovacs said the upper level will not be attached. K. Kovacs said there will be open 
terraces on the upper levels. K. Kovacs said they will review what is necessary to preserve the 
church such as masonry and windows. K. Kovacs said there will be green rooms and recording 
studios on the back side of the site as well. K. Kovacs said the plan is to clad the addition with 
stone and relate it with the church. K. Kovacs said the building will look to add signage via 
etching into the stone. K. Kovacs said the addition would be 1500 sf total, and the existing 
building is 13000 sq ft footprint. K. Kovacs showed renderings from different angles. 
 
Discussion: 
G. Villaras said when reviewing projects he reviews how it relates to past and future of Lowell. 
G. Villaras said the project does this effectively. G. Villaras noted the building has a scrolling 
design that relates to the use. G. Villaras said his only concern is the church has a presence on 
the corner, and expressed some concern that is being seen before the church and 
recommended it be setback a degree from the front so the Church is seen first. K. Kovacs said 
they will review what flexibility they have to adjust the location, and noted the design is a nod to 
the scroll. G. Vilalras noted everything is very compact along Merrimack Street.  
 
J. Sampas said they wanted the addition separated because the interest in creating a museum to 
honor the work. G. Villaras said just recommending it a few more feet down Aiken so the church 
is seen first. G. Villaras noted he feels both buildings look good.
